KEY MESSAGE 1: A potent cold front preceded and accompanied by an 
anomalously strong low-level WSW jet of 45-55 kts will move 
SE across PA today with a severe threat focused this
aftn/evening.

A surface warm front extending from KELM to KUNV and KAOO/KCBE
at 08Z will drift northeast across the Susq Valley and Eastern 
PA through the mid morning hours. This weather feature will 
bring a few periods of moderate to briefly heavy rain showers 
before a several hour lull in the rainfall occurs for the late 
morning and early afternoon hours.

The rather optimal timing of the break in the showers for much 
of the CWA during the late morning/early afternoon will allow 
for at least some air mass destabilization before a strong cold 
front begins to approach from the west. 

The HREF shows surface-based CAPE approaching 1000 J/kg for 
areas east of I-99 which will be more than sufficient for 
widespread thunderstorm development along the front in the high
shear/relatively low CAPE envir. 

With 925-850 mb West-Southwesterly winds averaging 45-55 kt and 
0-6 km bulk shear expected to be in the 40 to 60 knot range and
oriented nearly parallel to the surface boundary, initial
discrete cells should quickly merge into a low-topped, fast-
moving squall line containing mini-bows, capable of producing 
strong to severe wind gusts. SPC continues the wind-driven 
slight risk of severe TSRA over the approx eastern half of the 
CWA to highlight this threat.

We will also need to watch the leading edge of the line for
brief QLCS tornadoes (mainly over the Susquehanna Valley and
points east) as model soundings show between 20 and 30 knots of
0-1 km shear and over 100 J/kg of 0-3 km CAPE that may aid in 
stretching any vorticity. The threat will likely be maximized 
(although a much lower chance than the potential for damaging 
wind gusts) during the afternoon over southeast PA, and this is 
where SPC has included a 2 percent tornado contour.

-----------------------------------------------------------

KEY MESSAGE 2: Windy with the first snowflakes of the season 
possible on the higher terrain of the north tonight/Sat morning

The post-frontal pressure gradient is pretty tight with 10mb of
drop across the state tonight and Saturday morning. 50+KT winds
behind the cold front will stay AOA 6-7kft and soundings from 
both the RAP and the NAM show NW winds at the top of the mixed 
layer remaining below 40 knots. This should prevent wind gusts 
from getting any stronger than 35 or 40 mph and a Wind Advisory 
continues to be a low probability. 

850 mb temps over Lake Erie will fall to around -5C by Saturday
morning as a much colder air mass moves in. This is certainly 
cold enough to support lake effect clouds with lake surface 
temps still in the low 60s, but the potential for widespread 
rain or snow showers continues to decrease.

Northerly flow will result in a very short fetch across the 
lakes, so moisture will be greatly limited. Even though model 
RH profiles do show saturation in the DGZ, significantly drier 
air below that level should prevent much of the precipitation 
from reaching the ground. That being said, most models do still 
show a few light rain or snow showers developing over the 
northern tier. The window of opportunity for these showers will 
be rather short as drier air moves in by mid-morning.
------------------------------------------------------------

KEY MESSAGE 3: Cold weather may end the growing season for many
places Sun morning. 

A large surface high moves in for the weekend, supplying dry 
but cold weather for Saturday and Sunday. Saturday will hold 
the coldest daytime temps with temps getting just above 40F in 
the NE and 52F in the SE. Those maxes will be 20-30F lower than
Friday's maxes. 

The current forecast show temperature dropping below freezing
Saturday morning over parts of northwest PA, but there is still
some uncertainty regarding just how low temperatures get since
it should stay pretty cloudy for much of the night. If
confidence continues to increase in parts of the region dipping
below 32, a Freeze Warning may be needed for some zones across
north-central PA. McKean County would be left out of any freeze
products since their growing season has already ended. Frost is
less of a concern Friday night/Saturday morning due to the
aforementioned cloud cover as well as the fact that winds 
likely stay pretty gusty.

Sunday morning will be the most-likely time for sub-freezing 
temps across much of the CWA. This could end the growing season
for a significant portion of the forecast area. A widespread 
frost is almost a certainty as winds decrease and go mainly calm
Sun AM. We'll be considering appropriate frost/freeze products,
but it is still too early to be that confident on details.
Sunday night will likely also feature fairly widespread frost,
but the location of any frost/freeze headlines will depend on 
where the growing season remains active after the previous
night's freeze.

H
